scope: Focused literature review; not exhaustive or systematic

records.title: An Autonomous Doppler Sodar Wind Profiling System
records.journal: Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology
records.annotation: A two-year Antarctic deployment used solar/wind generation and batteries for an approximately 70 W active sodar. Available energy could not sustain continuous profiling. Halley personnel selected scientifically interesting meteorological situations and battery-supported observing intervals, usually 12–48 hours. This is a direct precedent for conserving energy for valuable atmospheric observations. Selection was operator-mediated using current conditions and battery voltage; it was not a demonstrated automatic forecast-and-battery optimizer.
records.evidence_depth: Full paper, especially pp. 1312–1315, power architecture and sounding criteria; field profiles and failures are reported. Metadata checked against the UEA author repository and journal information.
records.study_setting: Atmospheric or polar field observations; see annotation

records.title: Cloud and precipitation properties from ground-based remote-sensing instruments in East Antarctica
records.annotation: HYDRANT combined ceilometer, precipitation radar, infrared measurements and surface meteorology at Princess Elisabeth Antarctica, a predominantly wind/solar-powered station remotely controlled outside summer. The study reports 14 months of cloud and 26 months of snowfall observations during 2010–2013; power failures interrupted winter cloud measurements. The ceilometer's typical total consumption was 310 W, versus 25 W for the unheated MRR. This is a close same-domain renewable-power comparator, but station infrastructure and remote control are distinct from a stand-alone autonomous scheduler.
records.evidence_depth: Full paper: station and operating context pp. 287–288; instrument power Tables 2 and 4; actual scientific results. No forecast-based allocation of energy among observing priorities is demonstrated in this paper.
records.study_setting: Atmospheric or polar field observations; see annotation

records.title: A Compact Rayleigh Autonomous Lidar (CORAL) for the middle atmosphere
records.annotation: CORAL automatically starts, stops and recovers using local weather, all-sky images, ECMWF forecasts and lidar returns. It obtained temperature profiles on 243 of 365 nights in southern Argentina during October 2019–October 2020. This establishes forecast-informed autonomous operation of a substantial atmospheric remote-sensing instrument. Its observing suitability logic is transferable, but electrical power is externally supplied; the result does not demonstrate renewable-energy forecasting, battery allocation, or scientific prioritization across multiple instruments.
records.evidence_depth: Full paper, abstract and software/observing examples; introduction explicitly retains electrical-power infrastructure. Do not misread the quoted 2.4 kW cooling capacity as electrical consumption.
records.study_setting: Atmospheric or polar field observations; see annotation

records.title: An autonomous adaptive low-power instrument platform (AAL-PIP) for remote high-latitude geospace data collection
records.journal: Geoscientific Instrumentation, Methods and Data Systems
records.annotation: Solar/battery Antarctic platforms retain low-power magnetic observations while scheduling the more demanding GPS receiver and reducing winter telemetry. The paper reports field engineering records and actual scheduled GPS observations; low battery charge leads to hibernation. It also describes instrument triggering from monitored magnetic conditions. That trigger capability is not separately validated by a documented autonomous-trigger event. The five-year unattended lifetime is a design target. Scientific-selection principles transfer, but these are low-power geospace instruments, not high-power cloud profilers.
records.evidence_depth: Full paper: pp. 212–213, operating policies; Fig. 4, January 2011–February 2014 engineering record; Figs. 15–16 and p. 225, field observations and winter limits.
records.study_setting: Atmospheric or polar field observations; see annotation

records.title: High and Dry: New Observations of Tropospheric and Cloud Properties above the Greenland Ice Sheet
records.journal: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society
records.annotation: ICECAPS at Summit combines active and passive remote sensors with radiosondes to characterize clouds and atmospheric structure over Greenland. Its first 20 months revealed year-round liquid cloud occurrence and seasonal moisture/cloud/snowfall variation. It is a strong science and instrument-integration precedent for linking atmospheric observations to ice-sheet mass and energy budgets. This article is not evidence for an off-grid, renewable-powered or autonomously science-prioritized observatory; Summit's supporting station infrastructure matters to the comparison.
records.evidence_depth: Publisher abstract and metadata verified through search indexing; direct publisher opening returned HTTP 403. Author NOAA bibliography confirms complete author order, year, pages and DOI. Detailed engineering/full-text assertions were not extracted from this source.
records.study_setting: Atmospheric or polar field observations; see annotation

records.title: Radar and ground-level measurements of clouds and precipitation collected during the POPE 2020 campaign at Princess Elisabeth Antarctica
records.annotation: The 2019–2020 campaign deployed a 94 GHz cloud radar near the station and three lower-power precipitation radars at remote sites without connection to its grid. Instrument placement reflected power and access requirements. A scanning X-band radar was usually started manually before precipitation events. This is a useful same-domain comparison of instrument-dependent operating costs and purposeful event sampling. The article does not establish the remote radars' generation technology or demonstrate autonomous energy-aware event selection.
records.evidence_depth: Full text, Sections 2.1–2.3, deployment periods and power/access constraints; public measurement dataset. Do not describe every radar as remotely powered or renewable merely because the campaign used Princess Elisabeth.
records.study_setting: Atmospheric or polar field observations; see annotation

records.title: PLATO-R: a new concept for Antarctic science
records.annotation: PLATO-R was deployed to Ridge A in January 2012 to provide heat, communications and up to 1 kW for astronomical experiments. Its engineering lineage combines fuel generators with summer solar generation, preserving fuel for winter. The paper reports earlier PLATO operation for 1235 uninterrupted days with annual servicing. This is a substantial autonomous polar-power comparator, but neither renewable-only nor maintenance-free; those long-duration results refer to earlier PLATO, not the newly deployed PLATO-R.
records.evidence_depth: Full peer-reviewed conference paper, introduction and system description. Useful engineering context across disciplines; it does not establish meteorological event selection or energy-forecast optimization.
records.study_setting: Atmospheric or polar field observations; see annotation

records.title: Power management in energy harvesting sensor networks
records.journal: ACM Transactions on Embedded Computing Systems
records.evidence_depth: Full text; published article
records.study_setting: Theory and evaluation using energy data measured with Heliomote prototype
records.annotation: Full text; mathematical models and evaluation with energy data measured by the Heliomote prototype. Source/consumption models, storage losses and adaptive duty cycles establish the energy-neutral principle. The algorithm holds energy to accommodate learning errors and lower-than-expected harvesting. This supports AURORA's general budgeting/reserve rationale. Prediction uses past harvesting profiles, not numerical weather forecasts; neither indefinite polar operation nor a particular AURORA reserve is demonstrated.
records.locator: sections 2–5, especially printed pp. 14–15 and conclusion p. 35.

records.title: Design, Modeling, and Capacity Planning for Micro-solar Power Sensor Networks
records.evidence_depth: Full text; institutional copy
records.study_setting: Environmental field deployment and capacity-model evaluation
records.annotation: Full text; HydroWatch forest watershed deployments and an urban comparison, with measured energy flows. Models connect panels, regulation, storage and application demand; the field results expose the importance of shading and seasonal supply. This directly supports site-specific generation/storage/load accounting. It is low-power micro-solar sensing and capacity planning, not meteorological-forecast scheduling or demonstrated prioritization of scientific events. Its numerical power/storage budgets cannot be transferred to AURORA.
records.locator: deployment description and empirical analysis, PDF pp. 2–3 and 8–11.
records.booktitle: 2008 International Conference on Information Processing in Sensor Networks (ipsn 2008)

records.title: Real-time scheduling for energy harvesting sensor nodes
records.evidence_depth: Publisher abstract only
records.study_setting: Formal scheduling analysis and simulation
records.annotation: Publisher abstract only for this exact journal article. Formal analysis and simulations combine task deadlines, harvesting behavior and finite storage; conventional earliest-deadline scheduling need not suffice. It supports the rationale for considering future energy and timing jointly when deciding whether to run tasks. Its optimality applies to its mathematical assumptions. This is not environmental field verification, a science-value objective, or validation of AURORA's scheduling policy.
records.locator: publisher abstract. Do not confuse the earlier conference paper with this journal article.

records.title: Leveraging weather forecasts in renewable energy systems
records.evidence_depth: Full text; published article on author institutional website
records.study_setting: Measured energy/weather sources plus trace-driven system case studies
records.annotation: Full text; measured weather/energy inputs and trace-driven case studies. Meteorological forecasts inform hour-to-day solar/wind energy estimates. The ViSE instrument testbed includes radar, but scheduling comparisons replay traces with scaled generation and assumed demand/storage. This strongly supports using forecasts to admit sustained observing tasks. It does not prove field-deployed forecast control throughout that evaluation, nor transfer prediction skill to AURORA.
records.locator: forecasting/model sections; ViSE evaluation on PDF pp. 8–9, including generation scaling and workload assumptions.

records.title: A utility-based adaptive sensing and multihop communication protocol for wireless sensor networks
records.evidence_depth: Full text; published article in institutional repository
records.study_setting: Glacier field-data-driven simulation of adaptive sensing and routing
records.annotation: Full text; adaptive sensing/routing evaluated in simulation using data and energy costs from deployed GlacsWeb glacier probes. Information gain and energy opportunity cost guide acquisition/communication. This supports explaining scientific usefulness as an allocation objective. The evaluated protocol is not a field demonstration of autonomous event targeting; it concerns battery-powered sensing, not forecast renewable supply. The authors acknowledge that reduced sampling can miss short events.
records.locator: sensing section; section 6.1, printed pp. 27:24–27:26, explicitly identifies simulations and field-derived data.

records.title: Value of Information Aware Opportunistic Duty Cycling in Solar Harvesting Sensor Networks
records.evidence_depth: Full author preprint; journal metadata independently verified
records.study_setting: Analytical model and simulations including measured SolarMote traces
records.annotation: Full author preprint; final journal bibliographic metadata independently verified. Theory and simulations, including SolarMote traces, allocate energy among harvesting/storage, sensing and communications according to data value. It supports the general choice between spending energy now and preserving it for useful future work. The data-value proxy does not equal a meteorological science objective, and no AURORA or field-control validation follows.
records.locator: algorithm and experimental sections, preprint pp. 10–12. Use 2016 journal year and all three authors; arXiv landing metadata differs.

records.title: An Energy Aware Adaptive Sampling Algorithm for Energy Harvesting WSN with Energy Hungry Sensors
records.evidence_depth: Full publisher text via indexed primary result; direct access intermittently rate limited
records.study_setting: Field-derived sensor energy data followed by MATLAB algorithm simulation
records.annotation: Full publisher text retrieved through indexed primary-source results; direct endpoints were intermittently rate-limited/challenged. Measured wind-sensor and beehive gas-sensor data parameterize MATLAB evaluation. Sampling changes with battery level and signal dynamics, including acquisition/warm-up costs. It supports accounting for operating modes and the information lost when conserving energy. The adaptive algorithm's reported performance is simulated using field data, not a deployed AURORA analogue.
records.locator: experimental evaluation and conclusion; aliasing is explicitly acknowledged.

records.title: DynaES: Dynamic Energy Scheduling for Energy Harvesting Environmental Sensors
records.evidence_depth: Full text; author PDF
records.study_setting: Trace-based simulation with measured hardware consumption
records.annotation: Full text; a trace-based simulator uses NSRDB/PVDAQ records and measured computing/sensor power costs. Predicted generation, sensor priorities and adjustable sensing intervals jointly determine energy use. This is a recent precedent for connecting budgets with domain-defined priorities. Predictions come from local histories, not online weather forecasts. Evaluation is simulation, not autonomous environmental deployment, and no numerical improvement or reliability guarantee transfers to AURORA.
records.booktitle: 2023 IEEE International Performance, Computing, and Communications Conference (IPCCC)

records.title: A dynamic programming schedule trading off quality and stability in task allocation for energy-neutral Internet of Things devices harvesting solar energy
records.journal: ITU Journal on Future and Evolving Technologies
records.evidence_depth: Full text; publisher PDF
records.study_setting: Real microcontroller implementation with simulated solar input
records.annotation: Full text; dynamic programming balances task quality and schedule stability under energy/battery constraints. The scheduler runs on an Arduino DUE, with simulated solar supply and prescribed tasks. It supports discussing continuity as a scheduling objective alongside utility. Hardware execution is demonstrated, but environmental field deployment and AURORA-specific minimum observing durations are not. Its stability metric is an analogy to scientific continuity, not a direct measurement of scientific value.

records.title: An application of the ECMWF Ensemble Prediction System for short-term solar power forecasting
records.evidence_depth: Publisher full-text sections and UCAR institutional record
records.study_setting: Three Italian photovoltaic plants; two years of observations; forecasts to 72 hours
records.annotation: Uses ECMWF ensembles with statistical correction to forecast solar power. It is a direct precedent for turning weather ensembles into generation estimates and correcting them against local measurements. The reported skill belongs to those plants and horizons; it does not validate a polar array or AURORA’s battery forecast.

records.title: Probabilistic solar forecasting: Benchmarks, post-processing, verification
records.evidence_depth: Publisher full-text sections and KIT institutional record
records.study_setting: Solar irradiance forecasting and verification at seven US SURFRAD stations
records.annotation: Compares probabilistic forecasts, post-processing and reference methods. This is the clearest citation for checking whether forecast ranges capture observations and outperform a meaningful baseline. A displayed ensemble spread alone is insufficient. Its irradiance evaluations do not establish the probability that a battery stays above a reserve throughout a multi-day schedule.

records.title: Probabilistic day-ahead forecasting of system-level renewable energy and electricity demand
records.evidence_depth: Publisher full-text results, discussion and methods; Crossref metadata
records.study_setting: California grid-scale day-ahead supply and demand forecasting
records.annotation: Studies joint probabilistic forecasts of electricity demand, solar and wind generation, including implications for reserve allocation. It supports considering uncertainty in both supply and demand. This is a grid-scale analogue with different data, decisions and constraints; it cannot supply a validated reserve policy or error distribution for AURORA.

records.title: Hybrid photovoltaic power forecasting by combining physical and machine learning models
records.evidence_depth: Publisher full-text sections; Crossref metadata
records.study_setting: Day-ahead photovoltaic forecasting at sites in Brazil and the Netherlands
records.annotation: Compares physical, statistical and hybrid models rather than assuming extra physical detail improves forecasts. Useful support for treating AURORA’s more detailed solar model as a candidate requiring independent evaluation. Results are specific to the two sites and tested models; they neither justify adopting the candidate nor demonstrate performance in Greenland.

records.title: Verification of solar irradiance probabilistic forecasts
records.evidence_depth: Publisher full-text sections; author and DTU bibliographic records; PDF retrieval unsuccessful
records.study_setting: Probabilistic irradiance verification in two contrasting climates
records.annotation: Explains complementary checks of forecast reliability, spread and overall performance, illustrated with two sites. Useful for designing the independent evaluation promised in the section. These are checks of irradiance forecasts, not evidence that AURORA’s current battery ranges are calibrated or that a schedule will remain feasible.

records.title: Nonintrusive appliance load monitoring
records.evidence_depth: Author bibliography and Crossref metadata only; original full paper not inspected
records.study_setting: Foundational appliance-load monitoring literature
records.annotation: Provides historical context for representing equipment through operating states. Retained as a discovery and background reference, not used to attribute a particular algorithm to AURORA. AURORA has measured outlet information and its own state and phase logic; household load disaggregation is a related problem, not evidence of the same implementation.

records.title: The added value of combining solar irradiance data and forecasts: A probabilistic benchmarking exercise
records.evidence_depth: Institutional abstract and published metadata
records.study_setting: Multi-climate benchmark of intra-hour and intra-day irradiance forecasts
records.annotation: Benchmarks probabilistic methods and finds value in combining ground, satellite and numerical-weather information. Useful recent support for testing inputs and simple baselines before adding model complexity. Its short forecasting horizons differ from AURORA’s multi-day planning, and it does not support describing unused weather-model slots as an operational blend.

records.title: Approximate Inference in Additive Factorial HMMs with Application to Energy Disaggregation
records.booktitle: Proceedings of the Fifteenth International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
records.evidence_depth: Official PMLR full-text PDF and bibliography
records.study_setting: Household electricity disaggregation using additive state models
records.annotation: Shows how multiple appliance states can explain an aggregate electricity signal. Useful conceptual support for learning recurring operating behaviour. It does not establish AURORA’s model structure, learned heater cycles or forecast accuracy. Keep the manuscript description tied to inspected project code and avoid calling it a hidden Markov model unless that is actually implemented.

records.title: The North Pacific Experiment (NORPEX-98): Targeted Observations for Improved North American Weather Forecasts
records.journal: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society
records.study_setting: Human-directed atmospheric field campaign; forecast-impact experiments
records.evidence_depth: publisher abstract only
records.annotation: NORPEX deployed targeted dropsondes and enhanced satellite winds to improve winter-storm forecasts. Initial impact experiments reported average benefits, but individual cases could degrade and the incremental contribution depended on other assimilated data. Human-run aircraft campaign; a precedent for scientific targeting rather than station autonomy, temporal power scheduling or demonstrated optimal observation value.
records.group: Adaptive observing and interpreting the record

records.title: Impacts of atmospheric river reconnaissance dropsondes on ECMWF Integrated Forecasting System precipitation forecasts
records.journal: Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society
records.study_setting: Atmospheric-river dropsondes; observing-system experiments with real field observations
records.evidence_depth: publisher full text
records.annotation: Observing-system experiments for two AR Recon seasons found benefits from targeted dropsondes, varying by region, lead time and assimilation configuration. Mission tracks considered meteorological structure and forecast sensitivity; some forecasts degraded. Supports evaluating whether a targeting strategy benefits its declared objective. It does not measure autonomous station energy management or guarantee that more targeted observations always help.
records.group: Adaptive observing and interpreting the record

records.title: Adaptive sampling of cumulus clouds with UAVs
records.study_setting: Adaptive cloud-UAV trajectory planning with energy/information objectives
records.evidence_depth: publisher abstract only
records.annotation: A proposed aircraft-fleet planner uses continually updated atmospheric maps to seek informative trajectories while exploiting airflow for energy-efficient flight. Evaluated in realistic cloud/aircraft simulations, not an operational autonomous cloud campaign. Useful conceptual link between science and energy objectives; do not transfer its performance to a fixed polar observatory.
records.group: Adaptive observing and interpreting the record

records.title: Adaptive Sampling of the Upper Ocean by Autonomous Floats During Atmospheric River Precipitation
records.study_setting: Forecast-informed ocean-float programming during atmospheric rivers; explicit ocean analogue
records.evidence_depth: publisher full text, especially section2.2.1
records.annotation: Forecast-informed float programming intensified sampling near predicted rain, then returned floats to their primary Argo mission. Battery preservation was an explicit design priority. The experiment detected short-lived upper-ocean responses. Ocean analogue, with daily forecast analysis and surface communication/programming; not evidence of fully autonomous onboard event selection. Even intensified profiles missed shorter-lived structures. This is the strongest precedent for balancing episodic science against sustained monitoring, not a quantified AURORA saving.
records.group: Adaptive observing and interpreting the record

records.title: Using Autonomy Flight Software to Improve Science Return on Earth Observing One
records.journal: Journal of Aerospace Computing, Information, and Communication
records.study_setting: Science-triggered EO-1 spacecraft planning and execution; explicit spacecraft analogue
records.evidence_depth: published full text hosted by NASA/JPL
records.annotation: EO-1 integrated onboard event analysis, resource-constrained replanning, command execution and independent fault protection as distinct components; science detection could request follow-up observations. Explicit spacecraft analogue. It illustrates that an observation recommendation is not equivalent to an operational closed loop. It does not establish AURORA control capability, safety or scientific return.
records.group: Adaptive observing and interpreting the record

records.title: Near-Optimal Sensor Placements in Gaussian Processes: Theory, Efficient Algorithms and Empirical Studies
records.study_setting: Information-based spatial sensor placement
records.evidence_depth: publisher full text
records.identifier_note: Publisher lists no DOI; 10.5555/1390681.1390689 appears in secondary ACM/dblp metadata but Crossref returns 404. Do not treat that identifier as a verified registered DOI. Canonical JMLR URL verified.
records.annotation: Sensor selection can target expected reduction in uncertainty about unobserved locations, rather than simply select the most uncertain location. The paper develops approximation algorithms and tests them on two datasets. Spatial design under specified probabilistic assumptions; neither a general definition of scientific value nor a ready-made event scheduler. Do not claim AURORA already uses this criterion.
records.group: Adaptive observing and interpreting the record

records.title: Geostatistical Inference Under Preferential Sampling
records.journal: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series C: Applied Statistics
records.study_setting: Preferential sampling of environmental fields
records.study_type: statistical theory, simulation and environmental biomonitoring
records.evidence_depth: published full text plus publisher metadata
records.annotation: When sample selection depends on the underlying phenomenon, ignoring that dependence can mislead inference. Simulations and environmental biomonitoring demonstrate the issue and a joint modelling approach. Primarily spatial statistics; application to time-selective AURORA operation is a design implication, not a measured bias estimate. It does not show that every adaptive design is biased or prescribe a background-observation frequency.
records.group: Adaptive observing and interpreting the record

records.title: Adaptive Cluster Sampling
records.journal: Journal of the American Statistical Association
records.study_setting: Adaptive cluster sample design and unbiased estimation
records.evidence_depth: publisher abstract only
records.annotation: Conventional estimators can be biased under observation-dependent expansion of a sample; the paper constructs design-unbiased estimators for its adaptive cluster designs. Supports wording about accounting for sampling choices, rather than saying selective operation necessarily introduces uncorrectable bias. Its estimators do not automatically apply to a battery-limited time series; the relevant inclusion/selection mechanism must first be defined.
records.group: Adaptive observing and interpreting the record

records.title: Adaptive spatial sampling design for environmental field prediction using low-cost sensing technologies
records.study_setting: Adaptive air-pollution sensor placement using utility and data quality
records.evidence_depth: author-deposited full manuscript plus publisher metadata
records.annotation: The design combines prediction uncertainty with a risk criterion; simulation experiments show that adaptive deployment benefits depend on sensor quantity and quality. Air-pollution spatial design and simulation, not an operational power-aware station. Useful for explaining why “scientific value” requires an explicit objective, while uncertainty alone is insufficient.
records.group: Adaptive observing and interpreting the record

records.title: Use of large-eddy simulations to design an adaptive sampling strategy to assess cumulus cloud heterogeneities by remotely piloted aircraft
records.study_setting: Adaptive cloud sampling evaluated against large-eddy simulation
records.evidence_depth: publisher full text
records.annotation: Simulated adaptive aircraft trajectories and spatial mapping were assessed against known cloud structure. Reconstruction depended on the number of aircraft, mapping method and the cloud's evolution; rapidly changing phases remained harder to capture. Simulation evidence for designing and evaluating an observing strategy, not real-world autonomous cloud flight. Supports testing whether a chosen sampling pattern represents the process of interest, rather than equating collected data volume with scientific completeness.
records.group: Adaptive observing and interpreting the record
